title: Other than for immediate administration, a practitioner dispenses controlled substances to an ultimate user only as sample medications
rule_summary: 105 CMR 700.010, Dispensing and Labeling of Sample Medications by Practitioners, provides at paragraph (A) that other than for immediate administration, a practitioner shall not dispense controlled substances to an ultimate user in the course of professional practice, except as follows: (1) a Schedule VI sample medication in a single dose or in such quantity as is in the opinion of the practitioner appropriate for the treatment of the patient but not exceeding a 30-day supply per dispensing, provided that this quantity may be increased to a 90-day supply if dispensed as part of an indigent patient drug program and deemed appropriate in the professional judgment of the practitioner; and (2) a Schedule II through V sample medication in a single dose or in such quantity as in the opinion of the practitioner is essential for the immediate treatment of the patient. Under 105 CMR 700.001, Sample Medication means a unit of prescription drug distributed by the manufacturer or distributor to practitioners in the original package from the manufacturer, not repackaged and given free of charge to patients, and such medications include, but are not limited to, those medications dispensed as part of an indigent patient drug program.
exam_relevance: Tests that, apart from immediate administration, a Massachusetts practitioner may dispense controlled substances to an ultimate user only as sample medications, that a Schedule II through V sample is limited to a single dose or the quantity essential for immediate treatment, and what counts as a sample medication.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations
authority.section: 105 CMR 700.010(A), read with the definition of Sample Medication in 105 CMR 700.001

numeric_facts.fact: maximum supply per dispensing of a Schedule VI sample medication by a practitioner
numeric_facts.conditions: may be increased to a 90-day supply if dispensed as part of an indigent patient drug program and deemed appropriate in the professional judgment of the practitioner

exceptions: The bar is stated as applying other than for immediate administration.
A Schedule II through V sample medication may be dispensed in a single dose or in such quantity as in the opinion of the practitioner is essential for the immediate treatment of the patient.
common_confusions: Treating a supply a practitioner hands a patient from the office's own stock as a sample medication, when a sample medication is a unit distributed by the manufacturer or distributor in the original package and given free of charge.
Reading the bar as reaching immediate administration, which the paragraph excepts.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-16 in the current text of 105 CMR 700.000 published by the Department of Public Health on mass.gov (the 39-page edition whose PDF was generated on 2024-02-02), including 105 CMR 700.010(A) and the definition of Sample Medication in 105 CMR 700.001.
